# Research 2 — Phase 1 v2 Multi-Horizon Robustness Report (K = 2, 3, 5)

**Generated by**: `scripts/05_build_v2_features_labels.py`  
**Source table**: `data/processed/frames_with_features.csv` (Phase 1 v1)  
**Output tables**:  
  - `data/processed/frames_v2_lagged_k2.csv` (K=2, ~66 ms horizon)  
  - `data/processed/frames_v2_lagged_k3.csv` (K=3, ~99 ms horizon)  
  - `data/processed/frames_v2_lagged_k5.csv` (K=5, ~165 ms horizon — primary modeling dataset)  
**Configuration**: `configs/phase0_config.yaml` (`labeling.forward_window_frames_variants: [2, 3, 5]`)

---

## Executive Summary

This robustness report evaluates the stability of the v2 forward-window labeling strategy across three different forward horizons: **K = 2 frames** (~66 ms), **K = 3 frames** (~99 ms), and **K = 5 frames** (~165 ms, the primary dataset). The backward feature lag window is kept strictly invariant at {0, 1, 2, 3, 5} across all three datasets, isolating the effect of label horizon selection.

Key takeaways from the multi-horizon evaluation:
- **Monotonic and Proportionate Scaling**: The positive failure rate scales smoothly and monotonically with forward horizon length: **8.88%** (single-frame baseline) $\to$ **21.88%** (K=2) $\to$ **26.48%** (K=3) $\to$ **33.79%** (K=5). There are no sudden non-linear jumps or degenerate regime shifts.
- **Cross-Family Stability**: The relative ranking of flight families by failure prevalence is preserved across all three K horizons. Highly dynamic families (F1, F3, F6) consistently exhibit the highest forward failure probabilities, while low-rotation families (F2, F11) remain lowest.
- **High Sample Retention**: Because only trailing frames are affected by K, sample retention remains above **98.5%** in all cases (21,717 rows for K=2, 21,684 rows for K=3, 21,618 rows for K=5).
- **K=5 Primary Dataset Identity**: `frames_v2_lagged_k5.csv` was verified by exact SHA-256 hash comparison and cell-by-cell diff to be **100% bitwise identical** to the pre-existing `frames_v2_lagged.csv`.

## 1. Horizon Comparison: Overall Statistics

| Horizon Variant | Temporal Horizon (dt=33ms) | Start Dropped / Flight | End Dropped / Flight | Total Dropped | Retained Frames | Retention % | Positive Frames | Positive Rate (%) | Growth vs. Single-Frame |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| *Single-Frame (Ref)* | 0 ms (same frame) | 5 | 5 | 330 | 21,618 | 98.50% | 1,920 | 8.88% | 1.00x |
| **K = 2** | ~66 ms (2 frames) | 5 | 2 | 231 | 21,717 | 98.95% | 4,751 | **21.88%** | **2.47x** |
| **K = 3** | ~99 ms (3 frames) | 5 | 3 | 264 | 21,684 | 98.80% | 5,743 | **26.48%** | **2.99x** |
| **K = 5** | ~165 ms (5 frames) | 5 | 5 | 330 | 21,618 | 98.50% | 7,304 | **33.79%** | **3.80x** |

## 2. Positive-Rate Breakdown by Flight Family

The table below compares the failure rate across all 11 flight families across horizons. Notice the consistent, monotonic progression from single-frame through K=2, K=3, and K=5 across all families.

| Family | Description / Maneuver Type | Single-Frame % | K=2 % (~66ms) | K=3 % (~99ms) | K=5 % (~165ms) | Overall Trend |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **F1** | High-speed aggressive forward-backward translation | 18.74% | 38.55% | 42.70% | 48.32% | Monotonic increase |
| **F2** | Smooth low-velocity linear survey trajectory | 3.20% | 8.94% | 11.43% | 15.85% | Monotonic increase |
| **F3** | Exploratory diagonal traverse with abrupt yaw adjustments | 14.33% | 38.08% | 46.40% | 58.90% | Monotonic increase |
| **F4** | Moderate-speed lawnmower pattern | 8.84% | 20.36% | 24.07% | 29.68% | Monotonic increase |
| **F5** | Continuous circular orbit with outward-facing yaw | 9.50% | 21.76% | 25.68% | 31.45% | Monotonic increase |
| **F6** | Aggressive yaw oscillations (pirouette stress test) | 8.79% | 25.67% | 33.23% | 45.09% | Monotonic increase |
| **F7** | Exploratory figure-8 pattern with variable pitch/roll | 9.62% | 21.78% | 25.54% | 30.59% | Monotonic increase |
| **F8** | Exploratory stepped elevation survey | 9.17% | 21.11% | 24.76% | 30.37% | Monotonic increase |
| **F9** | High-yaw rotational sweeps (VFO lead-lag testbed) | 6.82% | 19.74% | 25.32% | 34.81% | Monotonic increase |
| **F10** | High-acceleration multi-axis pirouette | 5.74% | 17.00% | 22.36% | 32.38% | Monotonic increase |
| **F11** | Gentle baseline hovering survey | 2.89% | 8.30% | 10.91% | 15.95% | Monotonic increase |

## 4. Verification: K=5 Dataset Identity Check

A strict validation check was executed to guarantee that generating K=2 and K=3 variants did not introduce any regression, drift, or discrepancy into the primary K=5 dataset.

- **Reference File**: `frames_v2_lagged.csv`
- **Newly Generated File**: `frames_v2_lagged_k5.csv`
- **Reference File SHA-256**: `6ecd093118fa9dbc3cffe404ff8555978e4f8e7098d523c6feb6d93e5803b262`
- **New File SHA-256**:       `6ecd093118fa9dbc3cffe404ff8555978e4f8e7098d523c6feb6d93e5803b262`
- **SHA-256 Hashes Match**:   **True**
- **DataFrame Exact Cell-by-Cell Equality (`pandas.equals`)**: **True**
- **Row Count Match**: **True** (21,618 rows)
- **Column Count Match**: **True** (20 columns)

> [!NOTE]
> `frames_v2_lagged_k5.csv` is 100% bitwise identical to `frames_v2_lagged.csv`. > Both files coexist in `data/processed/` to ensure full backward compatibility with any script > expecting `frames_v2_lagged.csv` while maintaining standard variant naming `frames_v2_lagged_k{K}.csv`.

## Next Steps

1. All three horizon datasets (`frames_v2_lagged_k2.csv`, `frames_v2_lagged_k3.csv`, `frames_v2_lagged_k5.csv`) are successfully built and verified.
2. K=5 remains the locked primary dataset for Phase 2 feature inspection and Phase 3 modeling.
3. K=2 and K=3 remain available as zero-cost robustness benchmarks to verify whether model behavior generalizes across forecast horizons.
